purpose: Machine-readable RPSGT V3 coverage/current-authority gap queue derived from the 2026-08-08 12-task and D2A audits. Gaps are implementation priorities, not learner score predictions.

taskGaps.gap: Full licensed current ICSD-3-TR exact-page map
taskGaps.nextAction: Obtain licensed current ICSD-3-TR and build exact-page disease/criteria map. Until then, keep older ICSD-3 page locators explicitly legacy and require the current TR/current-guideline overlay.

Route oral appliance, surgical referral, upper-airway stimulation, transvenous phrenic nerve stimulation, and other non-PAP therapies by indication. Use current authority first and preserve unresolved upper-airway-stimulation sourcing as a gap.

Build oxygen-by-indication routing for ordered low-flow oxygen, CSA/high-altitude/heart-failure context, PAP titration, hypoventilation/CO2 monitoring, safety, and documentation. Do not invent a universal oxygen titration protocol.

Create an AASM-v3-first crosswalk for montage/setup, staging, arousals, respiratory events, CO2, MSLT preparation, age-specific care, and documentation. Do not treat AAST Standard PSG as pediatric PSG guidance.
Separate OSA PAP, CSA/ASV, and hypoventilation/NIV pathways using current AASM treatment guidance, AAST technical workflow, orders, facility SOPs, and manufacturer instructions.
Use a universal recognize -> verify patient/signal -> document -> allowed technical correction -> escalate per policy framework. Keep emergency thresholds and facility configuration local.
Locate and verify the actual current third edition before mapping. Do not relabel the older library copy.

taskGaps.gap: Adult Principles and Practice exact page locators
taskGaps.nextAction: Add exact page ranges only after reliable access to the oversized source. Do not guess.
Keep provenance/answer-key metadata out of official task counts, study surfaces, practice generation, and learner-facing imports.

d2aGaps.action: Create an original SPG pediatric technical-prep module cross-walking AASM v3 infant/pediatric rules, current pediatric MSLT guidance, AAST age-specific competency, and facility policies. Use pediatric textbooks/atlases only as support.
Require physician order + facility oxygen protocol + current AAST competency/scope + applicable AASM treatment/scoring guidance. Avoid a universal titration protocol.
Require manufacturer/facility SOP overlays for device-specific calibration and cleaning rather than treating general guidelines or textbooks as device instructions.
Split OSA PAP, CSA/ASV, and hypoventilation/NIV preparation pathways.
Teach universal principles and require manufacturer instructions for device-specific operation.
Keep technical camera positioning separate from local consent, privacy, retention, and storage policy.
